subject: segfault while drawing the plots for a paired analysis following the  vignette 5.0/6.0

messages.author: a9a4411b6693c26f
messages.subject: segfault while drawing the plots for a paired analysis following the  vignette 5.0/6.0
parts:
Hi all,
I installed aroma.affymetrix a couple of days ago and wanted to try a paired analysis with a very small data set: 2 cancerous samples and the 2 corresponding normals. I followed the vignette for 5.0/6.0. In the step for fitting copy-number model, I got a segfault while draqing the plots. R quit. Then following the suggestions given before, I deleted 'reports/ICGC/6.0,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY,paired/' and ran the same script.This time, another segfault caught but R didnt quit. Finally I checked the pngs in

reports/ICGC/6.0,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY,paired/GenomeWideSNP_6/cbs/01TD-GenomeWideSNP6

All seems fine except the one for 64X. I cannot open it , it seems to be corrupt. 
Am I doing anything wrong? There shouldnt be any problems with the small sample size, right?


Gunes




Here is what I ran:

##########################################################################
library(aroma.affymetrix)
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8, timestamp=TRUE)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6", tags="Full")
gi <- getGenomeInformation(cdf)
si <- getSnpInformation(cdf)
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("ICGC,6.0,testSet", cdf=cdf)
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=+300)

if (length(findUnitsTodo(plm)) > 0) {
   # Fit CN probes quickly (~5-10s/array + some overhead)
  units <- fitCnProbes(plm, verbose=verbose)
  str(units)
  # int [1:945826] 935590 935591 935592 935593 935594 935595 ...

  # Fit remaining units, i.e. SNPs (~5-10min/array)
  units <- fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
  str(units)
}

ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces)
cesN <- process(fln, verbose=verbose)
cesC <- extract(cesN, c(1,2)) ## test arrays
cesT <- extract(cesN, c(4,3)) ## control arrays
cbs <- CbsModel(cesT, cesC)
ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(cbs)
process(ce, arrays=1, chromosomes=1, verbose=verbose)
##########################################################################

On Fri, Aug 21, 2009 at 12:51 AM, gunes gundem<gugu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
> I installed aroma.affymetrix a couple of days ago and wanted to try a paired
> analysis with a very small data set: 2 cancerous samples and the 2
> corresponding normals. I followed the vignette for 5.0/6.0.

FYI: It looks like you are using the "old" vignette "Total Copy Number
Analysis (5.0 & 6.0)". FYI, the "new" one named "Estimation of total
copy numbers using the CRMA v2 method (10K-6.0)" will give better
results:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/estimation-of-total-copy-numbers-using-the-crma-v2-method

where the CRMA v2 paper is:

H. Bengtsson; P. Wirapati & T.P. Speed, A single-array preprocessing
method for estimating full-resolution raw copy numbers from all
Affymetrix genotyping arrays including GenomeWideSNP 5 & 6,
Bioinformatics, 2009

> In the step for
> fitting copy-number model, I got a segfault while draqing the plots. R quit.
> Then following the suggestions given before, I deleted
> 'reports/ICGC/6.0,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY,paired/' and ran
> the same script.This time, another segfault caught but R didnt quit. Finally
> I checked the pngs in
>
> reports/ICGC/6.0,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY,paired/GenomeWideSNP_6/cbs/01TD-GenomeWideSNP6
>
> All seems fine except the one for 64X. I cannot open it , it seems to be
> corrupt.

From the "error" messages, it looks like your PNG device (driver) is
not working properly. This is a problem independent of
aroma.affymetrix. It has more likely to do with your R or Linux
installation.

Now, R provides many different PNG drivers, e.g. several via png() and
some via bitmap(), and aroma.affymetrix tries to pick "the best one".
It uses findPngDevice() for doing this. What do you get if you do:

library("aroma.affymetrix");
print(findPngDevice(transparent=FALSE));
print(findPngDevice(transparent=TRUE));

You can also trick aroma.affymetrix to use a specific PNG device by
overriding this function:

findPngDevice <- function(transparent=TRUE, ...) {
if (transparent) function(...) png(..., bg=NA) else function(...) png(...);
}

See also the Aug 18, 2008 thread 'ChromosomeExplorer memory leaks':

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/e06bc012b5359dea/e20e1698d2cd14e3?#e20e1698d2cd14e3

> Am I doing anything wrong? There shouldnt be any problems with the small
> sample size, right?

Nope. No, this has nothing to do with the number of arrays analyzed.

Cheers,

/Henrik
